heading: IOI circuit evaluations depend on ablation, metric and prompt distribution
definition: how faithful and complete the circuit looks depends on the ablation, metric and prompt distribution, and the circuit explains only part of the behaviour.
summary: Several independent groups find that circuit evaluations change with evaluation choices, with evidence extending to Llama and Qwen models. The circuit explains only part of the behavior, although some evaluation changes leave results stable.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for GPT-2 small at <1B and for condition-specific sensitivity at 1–10B; ? for toy, 10–100B and >100B. Much of the GPT-2 evidence is size-unspecified in the script’s buckets.
suggested_status.reason: Condition-dependent evaluation sensitivity is reproduced beyond the original study: reviewed GPT-2 evaluations show replacement and granularity effects (arXiv:2407.08734#R3; arXiv:2407.08734#R7) and ablation-dependent circuit loss comparisons (arXiv:2409.09951#r2; arXiv:2409.09951#r3). Prompt-transfer results extend to Llama and Qwen instruct models (arXiv:2605.09129#r5; arXiv:2605.09129#r7), and Qwen patching/ablation results show intervention dependence (arXiv:2608.03629#R9). counts: versions.V5.verdicts.supports.studies=25, versions.V5.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=3, versions.V5.verdicts.challenges.studies=1, and versions.V5.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=1. The status applies to conditional sensitivity, with stable settings retained as limits, rather than universal sensitivity to every evaluation choice. Scale coverage follows versions.V5.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.open_questions: A matched evaluation of the fixed manual circuit across ablations, behavioral metrics, prompt distributions and subset-search completeness would clarify the joint claim. Independent tests above 10B and in explicitly fine-tuned or reasoning-stage models would extend its scope. Repeating the CD-T mean/zero comparison alongside the manual circuit under identical evaluation conditions would sharpen the stated exception.

source.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
source.authors: Kevin Wang; Alexandre Variengien; Arthur Conmy; Buck Shlegeris; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: The authors evaluated the GPT-2 small attention-head circuit using ablations and searches over removed nodes.
original_result.result: The circuit retained 87% of the full model’s mean logit difference—the average output-score margin for the recipient’s name over the subject’s—a gap of 0.46. Differences between circuit and full-model responses to removals, measured by incompleteness scores, were small for random removals and removals of whole head classes; greedy searches for removals found differences up to 3.09, compared with the original logit difference of 3.56.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: MLP8's apparent contribution to indirect object identification (IOI) depended on the patching intervention and evaluation metric.
Mean ablation inflated faithfulness on IOI variants, while rediscovered circuits explained only part of behavior.
IOI circuit recovery depended on ablation and objective, and the canonical circuit underperformed the model.
Single-node ablations revealed IOI effects outside the circuit and distributed effects within it.
IOI knockdown conclusions changed with ablation, and the circuit failed equivalence tests.
IOI edge effects changed with intervention scope and measurement, sometimes reversing sign.
The manual IOI circuit appeared near-optimal only under optimal ablation.
Patching the inhibition subspace appeared nearly complete by a metric but much weaker by interchange accuracy.
IOI circuit faithfulness varied across evaluation choices and individual prompts.
Path-patching procedures and thresholds changed IOI circuit size and performance.
IOI component necessity and discovered circuits depended on prompt distribution, ablation, and discovery loss.
Sparse IOI circuits lost faithfulness when evaluated on other prompt variants.
IOI circuits retained substantial unfaithfulness, whose magnitude tracked metric normalization.
IOI circuit necessity depended on granularity, selection, and metric despite unchanged accuracy.
Heads that copy names appeared important under path patching but caused no drop under mean ablation.
Circuit stability and faithfulness varied with sampling regime and ablation.
The evaluation metric strongly changed which circuits met the faithfulness threshold.
OLMoE ablation left top-1 performance unchanged while reducing logit difference.
A circuit-level measure diverged from faithfulness and direct logit attribution across the tested models.
A method's IOI overshoot was rewarded by a metric but penalized by another.
IOI circuit evaluations depended on ablation and omitted heads needed to reproduce model errors.
IOI circuits nearly recovered gaps through patching but left substantial gaps after zero ablation.
Stricter ablation reduced the IOI circuit's apparent faithfulness.
Layer 8's apparent IOI patching importance changed with the corruption distribution.
Ablation and metric choices changed whether inferior IOI candidates outranked the published circuit.
Mean and resample ablation produced no significant faithfulness difference at edge level.
Zero and mean ablation gave similar necessity results across six tasks including IOI.
IOI circuit structure and faithfulness stayed fairly stable under meta-dataset and paraphrase sampling.
CD-T IOI circuits had comparable faithfulness curves under mean and zero ablation.

untested.what: How the original circuit’s subset-search completeness discrepancy changes jointly across ablation type, metric and prompt distribution.
untested.basis: The original varies subset search, whereas later full-circuit evaluations emphasize faithfulness, necessity or agreement. counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation.removal and versions.V5.main_rows_by_operation establish intervention coverage but do not establish this joint completeness comparison. Original references: arXiv:2211.00593#r12 and arXiv:2211.00593#r13.

wording_issues.issue: The evidence concerns different objects: the published manual circuit, separately discovered CD-T circuits, EAP-family edge circuits, and selected component subspaces. The CD-T comparison uses circuits obtained under different ablations rather than holding the reference circuit fixed; it does not directly test evaluation sensitivity of that reference circuit. Results should retain their circuit and granularity qualifications.

wording_issues.phrase: depends on the ablation, metric and prompt distribution
wording_issues.issue: Dependence is conditional. The manual circuit’s edge mean/resample contrast is nonsignificant. Meta-dataset or paraphrase sampling yields comparatively weak structural sensitivity and low circuit error for automatically extracted circuits; these results do not establish reuse of the original circuit’s components or heuristics. Comparable mean/zero curves for separately obtained CD-T circuits do not test sensitivity of a fixed reference circuit. A dependence claim need not imply a difference under every comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: explains only part of the behaviour
wording_issues.issue: Logit-difference recovery is a score ratio, not a proportion of behaviors explained. Ratios can exceed unity under ablation artifacts. For the manual GPT-2-small circuit under mean ablation, normalized faithfulness F=0.956, correct-answer agreement Aok=99.5%, and exact error agreement Aerr=15.2%; under ABC resampling, F=0.644, Aok=91.2%, and Aerr=40.6%. The behavior and measure need naming.

The original completeness criterion is a circuit/full-model discrepancy after removing circuit subsets. Component patching effects, recovery AUC, necessity and error agreement test related but distinct properties; they do not all directly evaluate that completeness criterion. A single recovery AUC also cannot determine V5 evaluation sensitivity; that requires comparisons across objectives or ablations.

method_sensitivity.factor: Replacement value, intervention granularity and token positions
method_sensitivity.what: Node resampling gives lower faithfulness than node mean ablation; edge mean/resample differences are nonsignificant. Ablating all token positions gives lower faithfulness than restricting ablation to circuit-specific positions. Stricter causal scrubbing also lowers reported recovery, with large uncertainty.

On GPT-2 small IOI, ACDC canonical-edge recovery AUC is 0.869 with corrupted activations and KL, 0.589 with corrupted activations and logit difference, 0.539 with zero replacement and KL, and 0.447 with zero replacement and logit difference. These matched comparisons demonstrate sensitivity; an isolated recovery AUC does not. Negative Name Movers are not recovered under the logit-difference objective, unlike recovery with low-threshold KL.

The original GPT-2-small study finds large incompleteness under greedy subset search, unlike random and whole-class sampling. Greedy incompleteness reaches 3.09, reported as 87% of the original logit difference. This is original-source baseline evidence.

Repeated-IO prompts expose mean-ablation S2 Hacking. Variant-specific edge circuits lose faithfulness on other IOI distributions, including Llama and Qwen instruct models. Template-split and mixed IOI give different results for core-excluding sheaves. Qualitative corruption sensitivity is observed: layer 8 matters under both switched-name and third-name corruptions and has the highest importance difference, with greater importance for third-name counterexamples.

For GPT-2-small EAP-family IOI circuits, bootstrap sampling is less structurally and behaviorally stable than meta-dataset sampling or paraphrasing. The latter regimes show comparatively weak structural sensitivity and low prediction mismatch, giving partial V5 evidence. For the published circuit under node-wise, token-specific mean ablation, averaging individual recovery percentages gives higher faithfulness than taking the ratio of average logit differences. Figure 4 varies ABC replacement-dataset size; faithfulness increases with that size.

Full MLP8, DAS-direction and rowspace-only patches produce different effects. For example, MLP8 DAS FLDD is 46.7%, but rowspace-only FLDD is 13.5%. FLDD and interchange accuracy also give different impressions of the same intervention.

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention route and whether other components can respond
method_sensitivity.what: Frozen-head path patching and joint mean ablation assign different apparent importance to GPT-2-small name movers; joint mean ablation changes logit difference from 3.484 to 3.520. For head (9,6), local ablation increases the IO logit while global ablation decreases it; local boosting of incoming signals decreases the IO logit. These comparisons show observed intervention sensitivity under V5. Qwen instance-specific patching recovery and zero-ablation collapse also diverge.

method_sensitivity.factor: Behavioral outcome, circuit selection and unit granularity
method_sensitivity.what: High mean-ablation faithfulness and correct-answer agreement can coexist with low exact error agreement. Top-1 accuracy can remain unchanged while name margins fall. Consensus versus per-example selection and component versus neuron granularity change necessity conclusions; the Gemma comparison changes selection and metric together.

method_sensitivity.factor: Faithfulness summary, normalization and ranking metric
method_sensitivity.what: CPR rewards MAttr overshoot while CMD penalizes it. CEAP reports IOI sensitivity to the |QG| normalization. Equal-size candidate rankings change with KL, LD or PD and the intervention used; metric-relative threshold acceptance also varies substantially. These results concern different operational definitions of faithfulness.

method_sensitivity.factor: Discovery thresholds, procedure and discovery-set composition
method_sensitivity.what: The APP verdict reports IOI circuits ranging from 13 to 115 heads and about 27% to 114% performance across thresholds. For GPT-2-small IOI, manual versus automatic path patching restores 75.58% versus 96.95% of the original average logit difference, demonstrating procedure sensitivity. In a separate ACDC follow-up, assigning existing errors 50% of discovery KL weight raises error agreement from 9.3% to 37.0%, while correct agreement changes from 98.7% to 91.0%. Using 500 error and 500 correct discovery examples instead changes error agreement from 9.3% to 44.2% and correct agreement from 98.7% to 91.4%. Model weights remain fixed during these discovery interventions.
